```{r} #| label: setup library(ggplot2) library(dplyr) library(grid) # sugarglider::add_glyph_legend() needs grid attached library(patchwork) library(sugarglider) library(cubble) oz <- ozmaps::abs_ste world <- map_data("world") pal <- list(ink = "#333F48", accent = "#BF5700", teal = "#005F86", sand = "#F8971F", base = "#ECEAE4", grid = "#9CADB7") theme_poster <- function(base_size = 14) { theme_void(base_size = base_size) + theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA), plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", colour = pal$ink, margin = margin(b = 6)), plot.title.position = "plot", legend.position = "bottom") } ``` ::: {.poster-header} ::: {.title-block} # Glyph maps for spatio-temporal data in R ### Seeing seasonality at every location with [**sugarglider**]{.pkg}, [**cubble**]{.pkg} and [**GGally**]{.pkg} ::: {.authors} Maliny Po^1^ · S. Nathan Yang^2^ · **H. Sherry Zhang**^3^ · Dianne Cook^1^ ::: ::: {.affil} ^1^Monash University ^2^Duke University ^3^The University of Texas at Austin [sugarglider is a Google Summer of Code project]{.gsoc} ::: ::: ::: {.header-hex} ```{r} #| label: header-glyph #| dev.args: !expr list(bg = 'transparent') #| fig-width: 3 #| fig-height: 3 #| out-width: "100%" aus_temp |> ggplot(aes(x_major = long, y_major = lat, x_minor = month, ymin_minor = tmin, ymax_minor = tmax)) + geom_glyph_ribbon(fill = "white", colour = "white", alpha = 0.9) + coord_fixed() + theme_void() + theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", colour = NA)) ``` ::: ::: ::: {.pcols} ::: {.pcol} ::: {.card .lead} ## Why glyph maps? Environmental data are often **many time series at many locations**: weather stations, river gauges, air-quality monitors, satellite grid cells. Small multiples lose the geography; animated maps lose the time series. A **glyph map** keeps both: each location's time series is drawn as a small plot (a *glyph*) placed at that location on the map, so you can read **local** seasonal shape and **global** spatial pattern at once [(Wickham et al., 2012)]{.cite}. ::: ::: {.card} ## How a glyph is built Each glyph has two coordinate systems: **major** (where on the map) and **minor** (the time series inside the glyph). ![](figures/diagram-transformation.png){width=78%} The minor axes are rescaled to $[-1, 1]$ and placed by a linear transformation: $$ \begin{aligned} x &= x_{\text{major}} + \tfrac{\text{width}}{2}\, x_{\text{minor}} \\ y &= y_{\text{major}} + \tfrac{\text{height}}{2}\, y_{\text{minor}} \end{aligned} $$ **Design choices that matter:** - **Global vs local rescale:** global lets you compare *magnitude* across sites; local makes the *shape* at each site visible. - **Reference boxes and lines** frame each glyph and give a baseline, which counters the Zöllner illusion of drifting lines. - **Glyph size** trades detail against overlap. ::: ::: {.card} ## A brief lineage ::: {.timeline} [2012]{.yr} **GGally::glyphs()**: computes glyph coordinates as a data frame that you draw yourself with `geom_path()`. [2023]{.yr} **cubble::geom_glyph()**: makes the glyph a ggplot2 *layer*, with `x_major`, `x_minor`, `y_major`, `y_minor` as aesthetics. [2026]{.yr} **sugarglider** [(R Journal)]{.cite}: adds **ribbon** and **segment** glyphs, which show an *interval* (e.g. daily min to max) over time, plus legends and themes. ::: ::: ::: {.card} ## Which one should I use? | | **GGally** | **cubble** | **sugarglider** | |:--|:--:|:--:|:--:| | Interface | `glyphs()` → data frame | ggplot2 layer | ggplot2 layer | | Glyph geometry | line | line | **ribbon, segment** | | Reference box & line | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | | Global / local rescale | via `y_scale` | ✓ | ✓ | | Polar glyphs | ✓ | ✓ | – | | Glyph legend & theme | – | – | ✓ | | Spatio-temporal data structure | – | ✓ | via cubble | | Interactive (ggiraph, leaflet) | – | via crosstalk | ✓ | ::: ::: ::: {.pcol} ::: {.card} ## GGally: the original `glyphs()` returns the transformed coordinates (`gx`, `gy`, `gid`); `add_ref_boxes()` and `add_ref_lines()` add the frames. Rescalers `range01()`, `rescale11()`, `mean0()`, `max1()` and `min0()` control what each glyph compares, and `polar = TRUE` wraps the glyph into a circle. ```{r} #| eval: false #| echo: true library(GGally) gly <- glyphs(nasa, x_major = "long", x_minor = "day", y_major = "lat", y_minor = "surftemp") ggplot(gly, aes(gx, gy, group = gid)) + add_ref_boxes(gly) + add_ref_lines(gly) + geom_path() ``` ```{r} #| label: ggally-map #| fig-width: 5.2 #| fig-height: 2.9 nasa_sub <- GGally::nasa |> filter(x %% 2 == 1, y %% 2 == 1) |> group_by(long, lat, month) |> summarise(surftemp = mean(surftemp), .groups = "drop") gly <- GGally::glyphs(nasa_sub, "long", "month", "lat", "surftemp", height = 4, width = 4.4) ggplot(gly, aes(gx, gy, group = gid)) + geom_polygon(data = world, aes(long, lat, group = group), fill = pal$base, colour = "white", inherit.aes = FALSE) + GGally::add_ref_boxes(gly, colour = pal$grid, fill = NA, linewidth = 0.2) + GGally::add_ref_lines(gly, colour = pal$grid, linewidth = 0.2) + geom_path(colour = pal$ink, linewidth = 0.45) + coord_quickmap(xlim = range(gly$gx), ylim = range(gly$gy), expand = FALSE) + labs(title = "Monthly surface temperature, 1995–2000") + theme_poster(12) ``` ::: ::: {.card} ## cubble: glyphs as a ggplot2 layer `geom_glyph()`, `geom_glyph_box()` and `geom_glyph_line()` take the major and minor variables as **aesthetics**, so glyph maps compose with any other layer (base maps, points, facets). They take a `polar`, `global_rescale`, `width`/`height` and `x_scale`/`y_scale` arguments. cubble's spatio-temporal data structure makes the wrangling easy: summarise in the **temporal** face, then `unfold()` the coordinates in before plotting. ```{r} #| eval: false #| echo: true library(cubble) climate_aus |> face_temporal() |> group_by(month = lubridate::month(date)) |> summarise(tmax = mean(tmax, na.rm = TRUE)) |> unfold(long, lat) |> ggplot(aes(x_major = long, x_minor = month, y_major = lat, y_minor = tmax)) + geom_glyph_box() + geom_glyph_line() + geom_glyph() ``` ```{r} #| label: cubble-map #| fig-width: 5.2 #| fig-height: 4.1 set.seed(2026) picked <- climate_aus |> as_tibble() |> mutate(cell = paste(round(long / 4), round(lat / 3.2))) |> group_by(cell) |> slice_sample(n = 1) |> pull(id) cb <- climate_aus |> filter(id %in% picked) |> face_temporal() |> group_by(month = lubridate::month(date)) |> summarise(tmax = mean(tmax, na.rm = TRUE)) |> unfold(long, lat) |> mutate(region = ifelse(lat > -25, "North of 25°S", "South of 25°S")) ggplot() + geom_sf(data = oz, fill = pal$base, colour = "white") + geom_glyph_box(data = cb, aes(x_major = long, x_minor = month, y_major = lat, y_minor = tmax, group = id), colour = pal$grid, linewidth = 0.2, width = 2.6, height = 1.8) + geom_glyph_line(data = cb, aes(x_major = long, x_minor = month, y_major = lat, y_minor = tmax, group = id), colour = pal$grid, linewidth = 0.2, width = 2.6, height = 1.8) + geom_glyph(data = cb, aes(x_major = long, x_minor = month, y_major = lat, y_minor = tmax, colour = region, group = id), width = 2.6, height = 1.8, linewidth = 0.5, key_glyph = "path") + scale_colour_manual(values = c(pal$accent, pal$teal), name = NULL) + guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(linewidth = 1.5))) + coord_sf(xlim = c(112, 155)) + labs(title = "Monthly mean max. temperature, 2020") + theme_poster(12) ``` [Southern stations swing strongly from summer to winter; tropical stations in the north stay hot all year with only a shallow mid-year dip.]{.takeaway} ::: ::: ::: {.pcol} ::: {.card .feature} ## sugarglider: intervals, not just lines sugarglider began as a **Google Summer of Code** project. A single line hides **variability**. Many environmental summaries are *ranges*: daily min–max temperature, quantile bands, uncertainty intervals. **sugarglider** adds two glyph geometries for them: ::: {.two-up} ::: {} **`geom_glyph_ribbon()`**
a band from `ymin_minor` to `ymax_minor` ::: ::: {} **`geom_glyph_segment()`**
a segment from `y_minor` to `yend_minor` ::: ::: plus the scaffolding for a readable map: `add_glyph_boxes()`, `add_ref_lines()`, `add_glyph_legend()` (an enlarged, labelled glyph to read the scale) and `theme_glyph()`. ::: ::: {.card .feature} ## sugarglider in action ```{r} #| eval: false #| echo: true library(sugarglider) aus_temp |> ggplot(aes(x_major = long, y_major = lat, x_minor = month, ymin_minor = tmin, ymax_minor = tmax)) + add_glyph_boxes() + add_ref_lines() + add_glyph_legend() + geom_glyph_ribbon() + theme_glyph() ``` ```{r} #| label: ribbon-map #| fig-width: 5.2 #| fig-height: 4.1 set.seed(28493) aus_temp |> mutate(across(c(tmin, tmax), \(x) x / 10)) |> group_by(id) |> mutate(prcp = mean(prcp, na.rm = TRUE)) |> ungroup() |> ggplot(aes(x_major = long, y_major = lat, x_minor = month, ymin_minor = tmin, ymax_minor = tmax)) + geom_sf(data = oz, fill = pal$base, colour = "white", inherit.aes = FALSE) + add_glyph_boxes(colour = pal$grid, linewidth = 0.2) + sugarglider::add_ref_lines(colour = pal$grid, linewidth = 0.2) + add_glyph_legend(fill = pal$teal, colour = pal$teal) + geom_glyph_ribbon(aes(fill = prcp, colour = prcp)) + scale_fill_gradient(low = "#9fdde2", high = "#005F86", aesthetics = c("fill", "colour"), name = "Mean monthly precipitation (mm/10)") + coord_sf(xlim = c(112, 155)) + labs(title = "Temperature range at 29 stations, 2020") + theme_poster(12) + theme(legend.key.width = unit(1.6, "cm"), legend.title.position = "top") ``` [Wet tropical stations have flat, narrow bands; inland stations show wide daily ranges and deep winter dips.]{.takeaway} ::: ::: {.card .feature} ## Global vs local rescale ```{r} #| label: rescale-maps #| fig-width: 5.2 #| fig-height: 2.6 seg <- function(global) { aus_temp |> ggplot(aes(x_major = long, y_major = lat, x_minor = month, y_minor = tmin, yend_minor = tmax)) + geom_sf(data = oz, fill = pal$base, colour = "white", inherit.aes = FALSE) + add_glyph_boxes(colour = pal$grid, linewidth = 0.15) + sugarglider::add_ref_lines(colour = pal$grid, linewidth = 0.15) + geom_glyph_segment(global_rescale = global, colour = pal$accent, linewidth = 0.3) + coord_sf(xlim = c(112, 155)) + labs(title = paste0("global_rescale = ", global)) + theme_poster(10) } seg(TRUE) + seg(FALSE) ``` [**Segment glyphs, two scalings.** Global scaling compares magnitudes across Australia; local scaling reveals each station's own seasonal shape.]{.caption} ::: ::: ::: {.pcol} ::: {.card .feature} ## Anatomy of a sugarglider map ![](figures/glyphmap-layers.png){width=100%} Every layer is its own function, so you add only what you need: a base map (`geom_sf()`), glyph boxes, reference lines, the ribbon or segment glyphs, and an optional legend glyph. ::: ::: {.card .lead .takehome} ## Take-home 1. A glyph map shows each site's **temporal shape** and the **spatial pattern** in one plot. 2. If your summary is a **range** (min–max, quantiles, uncertainty), use sugarglider's **ribbon** or **segment** glyphs. 3. Use **global** rescaling to compare magnitude across sites and **local** rescaling to compare shape. 4. All three packages work with **ggplot2**, so you can add base maps, colour and facets as usual. ::: ::: {.card .getstarted} ## Get started ```{r} #| eval: false #| echo: true install.packages(c("sugarglider", "cubble", "GGally")) ``` ```{r} #| label: qr #| fig-width: 7 #| fig-height: 2.3 qr_plot <- function(url, label) { m <- qrcode::qr_code(url) |> unclass() df <- expand.grid(y = rev(seq_len(nrow(m))), x = seq_len(ncol(m))) df$on <- as.vector(m) ggplot(df[df$on, ], aes(x, y)) + geom_tile(fill = pal$ink) + coord_fixed() + labs(title = label) + theme_void(base_size = 13) + theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", colour = pal$ink)) } qr_plot("https://doi.org/10.32614/RJ-2026-050", "Paper") + qr_plot("https://maliny12.github.io/sugarglider/", "sugarglider") + qr_plot("https://huizezhang-sherry.github.io/cubble/", "cubble") + qr_plot("https://ggobi.github.io/ggally/", "GGally") + plot_layout(nrow = 1) ``` ::: {.refs} Wickham, Hofmann, Wickham & Cook (2012). Glyph-maps for visually exploring temporal patterns in climate data and models. *Environmetrics* 23(5), 382–393. [doi:10.1002/env.2152](https://doi.org/10.1002/env.2152)
Zhang, Cook, Laa, Langrené & Menéndez (2024). cubble: An R package for organizing and wrangling multivariate spatio-temporal data. *J. Stat. Softw.* 110(7). [doi:10.18637/jss.v110.i07](https://doi.org/10.18637/jss.v110.i07)
Po, Yang, Zhang & Cook (2026). sugarglider: Create glyph-maps of spatiotemporal data. *The R Journal* 18(3), 286–304. [doi:10.32614/RJ-2026-050](https://doi.org/10.32614/RJ-2026-050) ::: ::: ::: :::

Use **global** rescaling to compare magnitude across sites and **local** rescaling to compare shape. 4. All three packages work with **ggplot2**, so you can add base maps, colour and facets as usual. ::: ::: {.card .getstarted} ## Get started ```{r} #| eval: false #| echo: true install.packages(c("sugarglider", "cubble", "GGally")) ``` ```{r} #| label: qr #| fig-width: 7 #| fig-height: 2.3 qr_plot <- function(url, label) { m <- qrcode::qr_code(url) |> unclass() df <- expand.grid(y = rev(seq_len(nrow(m))), x = seq_len(ncol(m))) df$on <- as.vector(m) ggplot(df[df$on, ], aes(x, y)) + geom_tile(fill = pal$ink) + coord_fixed() + labs(title = label) + theme_void(base_size = 13) + theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", colour = pal$ink)) } qr_plot("https://doi.org/10.32614/RJ-2026-050", "Paper") + qr_plot("https://maliny12.github.io/sugarglider/", "sugarglider") + qr_plot("https://huizezhang-sherry.github.io/cubble/", "cubble") + qr_plot("https://ggobi.github.io/ggally/", "GGally") + plot_layout(nrow = 1) ``` ::: {.refs} Wickham, Hofmann, Wickham & Cook (2012).
